stem.text: A particle moves in the xy-plane so that its velocity vector at time \( t \) is \( \langle x'(t), y'(t) \rangle = \left\langle \sqrt{1 + t^{3}},\; 4 - e^{t^{2}/4} \right\rangle \) for \( 0 \le t \le 4 \). At time \( t = 2 \) the particle is at the point \( (4, 1) \).

parts.prompt: Find the x-coordinate of the position of the particle at time \( t = 0 \).

worked_solution.text: The x-coordinate at t = 2 equals the x-coordinate at t = 0 plus the integral of x'(t) from 0 to 2.
Solve for x(0) and evaluate the integral on the calculator.

points.criterion: Writes the definite integral of sqrt(1 + t^3) with t = 0 and t = 2 as its limits.
Uses the known x-coordinate 4 at t = 2 by subtracting the integral from 0 to 2 from 4 (equivalently, adding the integral from 2 to 0 to 4).

parts.prompt: Find the greatest y-coordinate of the position of the particle for \( 0 \le t \le 4 \). Justify your answer.

worked_solution.text: Set the vertical velocity equal to zero.
The vertical velocity is positive before this time and negative after it, so y increases and then decreases on the whole interval and the only critical time gives the greatest y-coordinate.
worked_solution.latex: y'(t) > 0 \text{ for } 0 \le t < 2\sqrt{\ln 4}, \quad y'(t) < 0 \text{ for } 2\sqrt{\ln 4} < t \le 4

worked_solution.text: Recover the y-coordinate at that time from the known position at t = 2.

points.criterion: Writes the y-coordinate at the critical time as 1 plus the definite integral of 4 - e^(t^2/4) from t = 2 to t = 2 sqrt(ln 4), about 2.355.
Sets y'(t) = 4 - e^(t^2/4) equal to 0 and finds the critical time t = 2 sqrt(ln 4), about 2.355.

Argues that y'(t) is positive before the critical time and negative after it on the whole interval from 0 to 4, so that the only critical time gives the greatest y-coordinate on the interval (a candidates comparison with y(0) and y(4) also earns this point).

parts.prompt: Find the time \( t \) at which the x-coordinate of the position of the particle is 7.

worked_solution.text: The x-coordinate increases because x'(t) > 0, so it equals 7 once, after t = 2.
Solve the equation on the calculator.

points.criterion: Writes the equation 4 plus the definite integral of sqrt(1 + t^3) from t = 2 to t = T equals 7 (or an equivalent equation built from x(0) and a lower limit of 0).
Solves that equation to give t = 2.781.
